title: Multiverse Computing targets a $570m Series C at a $1.7bn valuation to cut AI costs
excerpt: Spanish deeptech company that shrinks large language models wants investors to bet that efficiency, rather than sheer scale, is where the next stretch of AI money gets made. Multiverse Computing, based in San Sebastián in Spain’s Basque Country, has opened a Series C round targeting up to $570m (€500m), the company said on July 27. […]
content_html:
Spanish deeptech company that shrinks large language models wants investors to bet that efficiency, rather than sheer scale, is where the next stretch of AI money gets made.

Multiverse Computing, based in San Sebastián in Spain’s Basque Country, has opened a Series C round targeting up to $570m (€500m), the company said on July 27.

The raise would value the startup at roughly $1.7bn (€1.5bn) before the new money arrives, which the company put at about five times its previous valuation.

The pitch rests on CompactifAI, a tool Multiverse says can compress a large language model by up to 95% with what it calls immaterial accuracy loss. It borrows tensor networks from quantum physics to strip redundancy out of a model, cutting the memory, cost, and energy each query burns.

The technique sits inside a broader compression race that has pulled in far larger players.

In practice, the company sells slimmed-down versions of open models such as Meta’s Llama, packaged to run on cheaper hardware or on-premises rather than inside a hyperscaler’s data centre.

That edge-to-cloud framing is the heart of the Series C pitch. As inference, the cost of actually running a model, overtakes training as the dominant expense for many buyers, the argument goes, they will pay for the same output at a fraction of the compute and power.

It is not the only use Multiverse has found for the maths. The firm, which began in quantum software, has applied the same methods to other problems, including a system to predict floods. The through line is squeezing more out of less, whether the target is a neural network or a river.

The round is co-led by Forgepoint Capital International, the BNPP Solar Impulse Venture Fund, and Bullhound Capital, according to the company. If it closes at the top of the range, Multiverse’s total funding would reach about $800m across all rounds.

The company has not said when it expects to finish raising, nor disclosed the terms attached to the lead investors’ stakes. A round that is announced while still open can also close below its target.

In June 2025 the firm closed a Series B worth €189m, or about $215m, led by Bullhound with backing from HP Tech Ventures, Toshiba, Forgepoint, SETT, and Spain’s CDP Venture Capital. Bloomberg reported in February that Multiverse was in talks at a €1.5bn valuation, the same figure now attached to the Series C.

Multiverse was founded in 2019 by chief executive Enrique Lizaso, a former banker, and chief scientific officer Román Orús, a physicist whose work on tensor networks underpins the product. Both the compression business and its quantum tools sit inside a wider European quantum push that has drawn heavy public funding.

Its customer list, per the company, runs to Iberdrola, Bosch, Telefónica, Allianz, Bank of Canada, Indra, and PwC.

Multiverse also reported steep growth to match its ambitions, claiming a tenfold rise in annualised revenue since the last round and first-quarter sales up 96 times year on year. Those figures are self-reported and have not been independently audited.

The bet is a distinctly European one. As models grow more expensive to run, a cluster of the region’s startups is chasing the inference bill rather than the frontier.

Data-centre electricity demand has become one of the industry’s hardest constraints, and trimming the energy a model burns per query is one of the few levers a startup can pull without owning chips or power stations.

Multiverse is selling the opposite trade. If the future of AI is smaller, cheaper, and closer to the edge, a compression startup on the Basque coast would rather own that corner than chase the frontier it is quietly trying to cut down to size.

content_html_zh:
西班牙深度科技公司缩小了大型语言模型的规模，希望投资者相信效率，而不是纯粹的规模，才是下一段人工智能资金的来源。

7 月 27 日，总部位于西班牙巴斯克地区圣塞巴斯蒂安的 MultiverseComputing 表示，该公司已启动 C 轮融资，融资金额高达 5.7 亿美元（5 亿欧元）。

在新资金到位之前，此次融资将使这家初创公司的估值约为 17 亿美元（15 亿欧元），该公司的估值约为之前估值的五倍。

该宣传以 CompactifAI 为基础，Multiverse 表示，该工具可以将大型语言模型压缩高达 95%，并带来所谓的非物质准确性损失。 它借用量子物理学中的张量网络来消除模型中的冗余，从而减少每个查询消耗的内存、成本和能量。

这项技术属于一场更广泛的压缩比赛，吸引了更大的球员。

实际上，该公司销售开放模型的精简版本，例如 Meta 的 Llama，打包后可以在更便宜的硬件或本地运行，而不是在超大规模企业的数据中心内运行。

这种从边缘到云端的框架是 C 轮融资的核心。 由此推论，实际运行模型的成本超过了培训，成为许多买家的主要支出，他们会以一小部分计算和功率来支付相同的输出。

这并不是多元宇宙在数学中的唯一用途。 该公司以量子软件起家，已将相同的方法应用于其他问题，包括预测洪水的系统。 无论目标是神经网络还是河流，直通线都是从更少中挤出更多。

据该公司称，本轮融资由 Forgepoint Capital International、BNPP Solar Impulse Venture Fund 和 Bullhound Capital 共同领投。 如果收于该区间的顶部，Multiverse 各轮融资总额将达到约 8 亿美元。

该公司尚未透露预计何时完成融资，也没有透露主要投资者持股的附加条款。 在尚未开放的情况下宣布的一轮也可能会低于其目标收盘价。

2025 年 6 月，该公司完成了价值 1.89 亿欧元（约合 2.15 亿美元）的 B 轮融资，由 Bullhound 领投，并得到了 HP Tech Ventures、东芝、Forgepoint、SETT 和西班牙 CDP Venture Capital 的支持。 彭博社 2 月份报道称，Multiverse 正在以 15 亿欧元的估值进行谈判，目前 C 轮融资的估值也是同样的数字。

Multiverse 由前银行家恩里克·利扎索 (Enrique Lizaso) 首席执行官和物理学家罗曼·奥鲁斯 (Román Orús) 于 2019 年创立，该产品的基础是在张量网络方面的研究。 压缩业务及其量子工具都属于更广泛的欧洲量子推动计划，该计划吸引了大量公共资金。

据该公司称，其客户名单包括 Iberdrola、博世、西班牙电信、安联、加拿大银行、英德拉和普华永道。

Multiverse 还报告了与其雄心壮志相匹配的大幅增长，声称自上一轮融资以来年化收入增长了十倍，第一季度销售额同比增长了 96 倍。 这些数字是自我报告的，未经独立审计。

这一赌注显然是欧洲赌注。 随着模型的运行成本越来越高，该地区的一批初创公司正在追逐推理费用，而不是前沿。

数据中心的电力需求已成为该行业最严峻的限制之一，而削减模型每次查询消耗的能源是初创公司在不拥有芯片或发电站的情况下可以使用的少数杠杆之一。

Multiverse 正在出售相反的交易。 如果人工智能的未来更小、更便宜、更接近边缘，巴斯克海岸的一家压缩初创公司宁愿占据这个角落，也不愿追逐它正在悄悄缩小规模的前沿。
